regime_classification.growth: {"dimension":"growth","metric_summary":"GDP 7.8%; PMI 54.6","signal_text":"India's headline 7.8% GDP is the press release; the real read is composite PMI at 54.6 — an 83rd-percentile print — while IIP slips to 6.7% YoY from 8.8% and core sector eases to 5.4%. Capacity utilisation at 77.4% confirms the investment cycle is genuine, not budgeted — but the deceleration in IIP against a still-elevated PMI suggests the services engine is carrying manufacturing. The inversion worth watching: if services PMI at 54.5 is doing the heavy lifting while manufacturing PMI falls to 52.8, India's growth quality is narrowing — and services-led cycles historically compress faster when global demand softens.","badge_label":"Slowing Pace","badge_type":"b-slow"}
regime_classification.inflation: {"dimension":"inflation","metric_summary":"CPI 4.45%; Fuel 22.93%","signal_text":"Headline CPI at 4.45% looks manageable until you decompose it — fuel inflation at 22.93% (95th percentile, up from 20.05%) is doing structural damage that the headline obscures. Core CPI at 3.9% sits at only the 28th percentile, which means the RBI's inflation forecast revision to 5.1% (from 4.6%) is almost entirely a fuel story — not a demand story. The second-order effect: WPI at 9.92% with fuel this elevated means producer margins are being squeezed before consumer prices fully adjust; the pass-through lag is 2-3 quarters, and the earnings season six months from now will reflect it.","badge_label":"Inflation Overshoot","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.credit: {"dimension":"credit","metric_summary":"Credit 17.1%; CD 81.4%","signal_text":"Bank credit at 17.1% YoY against deposit growth of 10.8% — a 630bps divergence — with CD ratio at 81.4% (75th percentile) is the structural fault line. NBFC credit growth accelerating to 14.9% from 10.6% signals that wholesale funding channels are being tapped as banks tighten retail deposit competition; the last time CD ratio sustained above 80% while credit grew at this pace was FY14, and within four quarters the system required emergency macro-prudential intervention. Credit card growth collapsing to 2.3% from 5.6% — while vehicle credit runs at 18.8% — suggests the regulator's prior risk-weight tightening on unsecured lending is biting exactly where it was aimed.","badge_label":"Deposit Gap Stress","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.policy: {"dimension":"policy","metric_summary":"Repo 5.25%","signal_text":"Repo at 5.25% with RBI's own inflation forecast now at 5.1% leaves a real rate of approximately 15bps — barely positive, and almost certainly negative once fuel pass-through completes. An extended pause is the only defensible stance, but the market is not fully pricing the asymmetry: if Brent holds at $104 through Q3, the RBI's forecast will need another upward revision, and the window for any accommodation closes entirely. For housing affordability, the average home loan rate at 7.65% (down from 7.9%) provides marginal relief — but with INR at 96.15 and imported inflation feeding through, the RBI is managing three variables with one instrument.","badge_label":"Rate Pause","badge_type":"b-neu"}
regime_classification.capex: {"dimension":"capex","metric_summary":"IIP CapG 16.1%; CU 77.4%","signal_text":"Capacity utilisation at 77.4% — up from 75.6% and now in the 74th percentile — crosses the threshold where private capex decisions historically accelerate; IIP capital goods at 16.1% YoY confirms the signal is translating into actual orders. The inversion: core sector at 5.4% (down from 6.0%) with manufacturing PMI slipping to 52.8 suggests the capex upcycle is concentrated in specific segments rather than broad-based — cement and steel dispatch data would confirm or deny, but the divergence between capital goods IIP and core sector is a yellow flag. If NBFC funding costs rise as the CD ratio stays elevated, the mid-market capex borrowers — who rely on NBFC credit — face a squeeze precisely when the investment cycle needs them most.","badge_label":"Capex Upcycle","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.consumption: {"dimension":"consumption","metric_summary":"GST 199853; PV 16%","signal_text":"GST at ₹1,99,853 crore is a strong print, but the YTD figure at the 14th percentile demands scrutiny — the monthly number may be capturing advance filings and formalization reclassification rather than pure demand expansion. Passenger vehicle sales at 16% YoY, two-wheelers at 19.7%, and commercial vehicles at 16.88% present a rare alignment across the demand pyramid: urban discretionary (PV), rural/semi-urban (2W), and freight (CV) all accelerating simultaneously. The divergence to watch: credit card growth at 2.3% — a 26th-percentile print — against vehicle credit at 18.8% suggests consumers are financing big-ticket purchases with debt while pulling back on revolving credit; that is a durability question, not a strength signal.","badge_label":"Demand Surge","badge_type":"b-exp"}

signal_cards.1: {"signal_num":1,"signal_theme":"CREDIT CYCLE","status":"risk","title":"Deposit Gap Forces RBI's Hand","data_text":"Bank credit growth at 17.1% YoY (Mar 2026) vs deposit growth at 10.8% — a 350bps divergence widening for three consecutive months. CD ratio at 81.4% (down from 82.5% prior month but structurally elevated). NBFC credit growth accelerating to 14.9% YoY, signalling wholesale funding pressure as banks tighten retail deposit competition.","implication":"Overweight private banks with CASA ratios >45% — they'll poach deposits from smaller peers. Avoid NBFCs with wholesale funding >30% of liabilities; liquidity stress will force asset sales or margin compression. RBI will likely signal deposit-friendly measures (higher savings rates, CRR cuts) within 6-8 weeks. Position for a 50bps rate cut by Q3 2026.","pct_10y":75,"pct_note":"CD ratio at 75th percentile historically precedes either RBI easing or a credit slowdown. Last time this divergence widened this sharply (2022), it resolved via a 200bps rate cut cycle.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.2: {"signal_num":2,"signal_theme":"CAPEX TRIGGER","status":"positive","title":"Capacity Utilisation Breaks Into Capex Zone","data_text":"Capacity utilisation at 77.4% (up from 75.6% prior month), now in the 74th percentile. IIP capital goods at 16.1% YoY. Core sector growth at 5.4% YoY (down from 6.0% but still positive). Manufacturing PMI at 52.8 (slight pullback from 53.5) but services PMI at 54.5, composite at 54.6 (83rd percentile — highest in 10 years).","implication":"Capex cycle is live but not yet frothy. Overweight capital goods manufacturers (Larsen & Toubro, Cummins, Bharat Heavy Electricals) and industrial automation plays. Avoid betting on a V-shaped recovery in core sector — the slowdown from 6.0% to 5.4% suggests commodity headwinds (oil, metals) are offsetting demand. Watch for order book commentary in Q4 earnings; if order inflows remain >15% YoY, capex will sustain through FY27.","pct_10y":74,"pct_note":"Capacity utilisation at 77% has historically preceded 18-24 months of steady capex. The last time it was this high (2018), capex growth averaged 12% for two years before moderating.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.3: {"signal_num":3,"signal_theme":"SIP / RETAIL FLOWS","status":"positive","title":"SIP Momentum Accelerates Into Affluent Territory","data_text":"SIP inflows at ₹32,297 Cr (up from ₹31,961 Cr prior month, rising 2 consecutive months). SIP AUM at ₹18.62 Tr (up from ₹18.21 Tr, rising 2 consecutive months). SIP accounts at 100.18 Cr (up from 99.06 Cr). Equity MF net inflows at ₹29,329 Cr (up from ₹24,697 Cr). MF AUM at ₹87.08 Tr (92nd percentile, rising 2 consecutive months).","implication":"Retail equity participation is broadening, not narrowing. The 14% YoY growth in SIP accounts masks a 25%+ growth in SIP AUM — average ticket size is rising, indicating affluent money entering via systematic routes. This is late-cycle behaviour. Overweight large-cap, dividend-paying stocks (HDFC Bank, TCS, Reliance) over small-caps. Reduce exposure to speculative micro-caps; retail euphoria typically peaks 6-9 months before a correction.","pct_10y":92,"pct_note":"SIP AUM at 93rd percentile is the highest in a decade. The last time SIP inflows were this strong (2021), they peaked 8 months before the March 2022 correction.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.4: {"signal_num":4,"signal_theme":"OIL / COMMODITY RISK","status":"risk","title":"Fuel Inflation Spike Threatens Margin Compression","data_text":"Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (up from 20.05% prior month, 95th percentile). Brent crude at $104.08/bbl (flat but elevated, 72nd percentile). WTI at $101.05/bbl (83rd percentile). FAO food index at 130.3 (up from 129.7, 57th percentile). CPI headline at 4.45% (up from 4.38%, 41st percentile). WPI at 9.92% (up from 9.78%, 67th percentile).","implication":"Fuel inflation is the primary driver of headline CPI overshoot. RBI's 5.1% inflation forecast (up from 4.6%) is now credible. This will delay rate cuts by 2-3 months. Underweight airlines (SpiceJet, IndiGo) and logistics (Allcargo, TCI Express) — fuel surcharges won't fully offset margin pressure. Overweight refiners (Reliance, HPCL) and energy stocks; they benefit from elevated crude. Hedge CAD risk via INR shorts; oil imports will widen the current account deficit.","pct_10y":95,"pct_note":"Fuel inflation at 95th percentile is a 10-year extreme. The last time it spiked this high (2022), it persisted for 6 months and forced RBI to hold rates steady despite growth concerns.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.5: {"signal_num":5,"signal_theme":"GLOBAL LIQUIDITY","status":"risk","title":"US Rates Sticky, BOJ Tightening Unwinds Carry","data_text":"US 10Y Treasury at 5.01% (up from 5.00%, 91st percentile, rising 4 of last 5 months). Fed funds rate at 3.63% (flat, 67th percentile). BOJ rate at 1.0% (up from 0.75%, 86th percentile — strong-negative signal). Fed balance sheet at $6,746.5B (flat, rising 2 consecutive months). US PMI composite at 56.0 (up from 54.5, 84th percentile). US GDP SAAR at 1.5% (down from 2.1%, 49th percentile).","implication":"The BOJ's rate hike to 1.0% is the canary in the coal mine. Yen carry trades are unwinding — expect volatility in emerging market equities and currencies. US rates are sticky at 5%+ despite slowing growth (1.5% SAAR), signalling the Fed will hold longer than markets priced. This is a headwind for India: FII flows will remain volatile, and INR depreciation pressure will persist. Reduce leverage in EM portfolios. Overweight INR hedges (long USD calls, short INR forwards). Expect 2-3 weeks of equity volatility as carry unwinds.","pct_10y":91,"pct_note":"US 10Y at 91st percentile with slowing growth is a regime shift. The last time this occurred (2018), it preceded a 20% equity correction and a 15% EM currency selloff.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.6: {"signal_num":6,"signal_theme":"INR / FX RESERVES","status":"watch","title":"INR Weakens as Carry Unwinds, RBI Likely Intervening","data_text":"INR/USD at 96.15 (flat, 91st percentile — near 10-year highs). Recent trend: 95.24→96.15→95.24→94.34→95.24→96.15 (up 3 of last 5 months, volatile). FII equity net at ₹29,631 Cr (up from ₹20,200 Cr, 83rd percentile, rising 1 of last 2 months). DII equity net at ₹58,502 Cr (100th percentile, rising 2 consecutive months). India VIX at 12.29 (down from 13.17, 7th percentile — complacency).","implication":"INR is at decade-high weakness despite strong DII inflows. This suggests RBI is intervening to prevent sharper depreciation (likely selling reserves). The BOJ carry unwind will pressure INR further — expect 96.50-97.00 levels in the next 4-6 weeks. DII strength is masking FII fragility; if FII reverses (likely if US rates stay at 5%+), INR will break 97. Hedge INR exposure via long USD forwards. Avoid INR-denominated debt; prefer dollar-linked returns. Watch RBI's next monetary policy statement for explicit INR defence language.","pct_10y":91,"pct_note":"INR at 91st percentile weakness with strong DII inflows is a classic late-cycle pattern. In 2018, this preceded a 6% INR depreciation over 3 months.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.7: {"signal_num":7,"signal_theme":"UNDER THE RADAR","status":"surprise","title":"Office Absorption Decouples From IT Stock Weakness","data_text":"Office absorption at 29.9 Mn sqft (up from 28.2 Mn sqft, 24th percentile — historically weak). Office vacancy at 13.9% (down from 17.2%, 38th percentile). Nifty IT index flat YoY. Bank Nifty at 56,055 (92nd percentile, strong-positive signal). Rent growth in Bengaluru at 100.6 (up from 93.8, 57th percentile). Rent growth in Mumbai at 125 (up from 117.9, 38th percentile). Retail mall vacancy at 11.9% (down from 12.3%, 39th percentile).","implication":"Commercial real estate is decoupling from IT services. Office absorption is rising despite Nifty IT weakness — this suggests Global Capability Centers (GCCs) and non-IT corporates (BFSI, consulting, startups) are the primary occupiers, not traditional IT services. This is a structural shift: IT services are consolidating headcount (hence flat stock prices), but GCCs are expanding footprints (hence rising absorption). Overweight commercial RE REITs (Embassy, Mindspace) on this thesis — they're pricing in IT weakness but will surprise on GCC demand. Underweight pure-play IT services; their real estate footprint is shrinking. Falsifiable: if Nifty IT rebounds >15% in the next 6 months without absorption accelerating further, this thesis breaks.","pct_10y":24,"pct_note":"Office absorption at 24th percentile is historically weak, but the composition has shifted. In 2019-2021, absorption at this level preceded IT layoffs. Today, it's masking a reallocation from IT to GCCs — a structural, not cyclical, phenomenon.","is_surprise":true}

executive_summary.1:
{"para_num":1,"para_label":"India Macro Regime","para_html":"

7.8% GDP with composite PMI at 54.6 — an 83rd-percentile reading — looks like a clean growth story until IIP at 6.7% (down from 8.8%) and core sector at 5.4% (down from 6.0%) reveal the deceleration underneath. Capacity utilisation at 77.4% validates the capex narrative — this is real investment, not budget allocation — but manufacturing PMI at 52.8 slipping while services holds at 54.5 means the growth engine is narrowing. Fuel inflation at 22.93% (95th percentile) with WPI at 9.92% is compressing producer margins two to three quarters before consumer prices fully adjust — the earnings risk is deferred, not avoided. Vehicle sales across all three segments running at 16-20% YoY confirm consumption breadth, but credit card growth at 2.3% signals the consumer is choosing asset financing over revolving spend — a durability question dressed as a strength signal.

"}
executive_summary.2:
{"para_num":2,"para_label":"Global Macro Regime","para_html":"

5.01% on the US 10Y — a 91st-percentile yield, rising four of the last five months — is the single most important global price today, and it is moving in the wrong direction for every EM carry trade simultaneously. US PMI composite at 56.0 (84th percentile, up from 54.5) with GDP SAAR at only 1.5% (down from 2.1%) is the classic late-cycle divergence: activity surveys still euphoric, hard output data already softening — the last three US recessions began with exactly this gap. BOJ at 1.0% (25bps hike, 86th percentile) is unwinding the last pillar of global carry, and with Nikkei at a 100th-percentile 64,136, Japanese equities are pricing a soft landing that the bond market — at these yields — is simultaneously pricing as structurally impossible. China composite PMI at 49.5 with GDP at 4.3% (down from 5.0%) removes the one demand buffer that could have offset US softness for Asian exporters.

"}
executive_summary.3:
{"para_num":3,"para_label":"Liquidity Conditions","para_html":"

DII equity net at ₹58,502 crore — a 100th-percentile print, rising two consecutive months — is absorbing every shock the global carry unwind can deliver, with SIP inflows at ₹32,297 crore and MF AUM at ₹87.08 trillion (86th percentile) providing the structural bid. FII equity net at ₹29,631 crore (83rd percentile) has turned positive, but the recent sequence — from -₹3,112 crore to +₹29,631 crore in a single month — is volatile enough to reverse on a single Fed communication. India VIX at 12.29 (7th percentile) against US VIX at 15.44 (9th percentile) is a complacency signal: domestic money is fully deployed, hedges are minimal, and the cushion against a global risk-off event is thinner than the flow data suggests. Bank credit at 17.1% against deposit growth of 10.8% means the system is funding growth through wholesale channels — and wholesale funding is the first to reprice when global rates move.

"}
executive_summary.4:
{"para_num":4,"para_label":"Equity + Real Estate Implications","para_html":"

Bank Nifty at 56,055 (92nd percentile) with CD ratio at 81.4% and deposit growth trailing credit by 630bps is the most precise valuation tension in Indian equities today — the index is pricing earnings that require deposit mobilisation the system is not delivering. Nifty50 at 23,271 (74th percentile) with India VIX at a 7th-percentile 12.29 means the market is priced for perfection with almost no insurance — a US 10Y at 5.01% sustained through October reprices EM risk premiums by 30-50bps and that flows directly into Nifty multiples. Office absorption at 29.9 mn sqft (24th percentile) with vacancy falling to 13.9% from 17.2% is a genuine improvement, but REIT prices tell the real story: Embassy down to ₹369.92 from ₹439.58, Mindspace at ₹345.06 from ₹498.78 — the physical market is tightening while listed vehicles are being de-rated by rising global yields. Retail mall vacancy at 11.9% confirms consumption is showing up in physical retail, but at these REIT valuations, the yield compression trade is over.

"}
executive_summary.5:
{"para_num":5,"para_label":"Key Risks to Monitor","para_html":"

Ranked by probability × impact: first, US 10Y sustaining above 5.0% through the next Fed meeting — at 91st-percentile yields with BOJ tightening simultaneously, EM carry unwinds are non-linear and India's ₹96.15 INR (91st percentile) has limited RBI intervention room without burning reserves. Second, fuel inflation at 22.93% feeding into RBI's forecast revision to 5.1% — if Brent holds at $104, the next MPC meeting closes the door on any accommodation and forces the RBI to choose between INR defence and growth support. Third, the CD ratio at 81.4% with NBFC credit accelerating to 14.9% — the macro-prudential response, when it comes, will arrive via risk-weight circulars on specific segments, and Bank Nifty at a 92nd-percentile valuation has no margin of safety for that event. Fourth, China PMI composite at 49.5 with GDP at 4.3% — a sub-50 composite in the world's largest goods exporter compresses commodity demand and removes the one external demand buffer for Asian supply chains. Watch the RBI's next liquidity management operation: if it shifts from variable rate repo to outright OMO sales, the policy signal will be tighter than the repo rate suggests — that is the single most important data point this week.

"}
